prompt: It is January 2, 2019. I would like to outperform the S&P 500 over the next five years. Can you propose 10 stocks I should buy? Answer as of that date.
reply:
# 10 Stocks to Beat the S&P 500: A Pick List as of January 2, 2019

**Caveat first:** My knowledge runs well past 2019, so I already know how the next five years turned out. Every reason below uses only information available in January 2019, but I can't guarantee hindsight didn't shape which names I picked. **Treat this as an example of the reasoning, not as proof that stock-picking works.**

## Market backdrop (Jan 2, 2019)
- The S&P 500 fell about 20% from its September high to its December 24 low, then closed 2018 near 2,507, its first down year since 2008.
- The main worries are Fed rate hikes, the US–China trade war, a government shutdown and fears of a recession.
- The selloff has made many high-quality growth companies cheaper. The idea is to buy durable businesses with pricing power while pessimism is high.

## The 10 picks

| # | Company | ~Price (12/31/18) | Why buy it | Main risk |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Microsoft (MSFT)** | $102 | Azure is growing ~75% a year, and Office has moved to subscriptions, so revenue is increasingly recurring. It has a huge cash pile. | Valuation (~24x forward earnings) |
| 2 | **Apple (AAPL)** | $158 | Shares are down about a third from October, at roughly 13x earnings. Net cash of over $100B funds buybacks, and high-margin Services revenue is growing 20%+. | iPhone sales are stagnating, it has stopped reporting unit sales, and China exposure is a trade-war risk |
| 3 | **Amazon (AMZN)** | $1,502 | AWS is growing ~45% with ~30% operating margins. Advertising is a new high-margin business. The stock is well off its highs. | Rich valuation, antitrust scrutiny |
| 4 | **Alphabet (GOOGL)** | $1,045 | It dominates search and YouTube, Google Cloud is growing, and Waymo is an extra option. It holds over $100B in cash. | EU fines and regulation |
| 5 | **NVIDIA (NVDA)** | $134 | Down over 50% from its October high because of excess crypto-mining inventory. Its GPUs are the standard for AI and deep learning, and new RTX gaming chips are just launching. | Clearing that inventory may take several quarters; the stock is very volatile |
| 6 | **Taiwan Semiconductor (TSM)** | $37 | It leads chipmaking with 7nm chips already in volume production while Intel's 10nm keeps slipping. About 15x earnings with a ~3.5% dividend yield. | Taiwan geopolitics, the chip cycle, reliance on Apple |
| 7 | **Adobe (ADBE)** | $226 | The move to Creative Cloud subscriptions is done, revenue is growing 20%+, and the Magento and Marketo deals expand its marketing software business. | Valuation, integrating the acquisitions |
| 8 | **Visa (V)** | $132 | It runs the largest payment network, with 50%+ net margins, and benefits as consumers keep shifting from cash to cards and online shopping. | Regulation, fintech disruption |
| 9 | **UnitedHealth (UNH)** | $249 | A defensive growth stock: Optum grows faster than the insurance business, and earnings have grown at double digits consistently. | "Medicare for All" talk ahead of 2020 and the court challenge to the ACA |
| 10 | **JPMorgan Chase (JPM)** | $98 | The best-run big US bank, at about 11x earnings, with strong capital returns and benefits from the 2017 tax cuts. | Recession and loan losses, a flattening yield curve |

## How to hold them
- **Weighting:** Put about 10% in each stock and rebalance once a year.
- **Concentration:** About 7 of the 10 are tech or tech-adjacent. That is a deliberate bet on dominant platforms, but it will lag badly if tech falls out of favor.
- **Time horizon:** Plan to hold all five years. The 2018 selloff shows these stocks can fall 30–50% even when the business is fine.
- **Set expectations:** Most professional large-cap managers trail the S&P 500 over five years. A sensible compromise is a "core and satellite" setup: most of your money in an index fund, with these 10 stocks as a smaller active bet.

*This is an educational exercise, not personalized financial advice.*

If you'd like, I can show how this list actually performed against the S&P 500 from 2019 to 2023. I could also build a rules-based screen that is less affected by my hindsight, for example "large caps with X growth and Y valuation as of December 2018."
